cr-1999:
Stretcher: "#13" (Alfred Stieglitz, graphite). Canvas edge: "#13" (unidentified hand, graphite). Backing: 1. OK {5star} (graphite) 2. "Line and Curve – 27?" (graphite) 3. "O'Keeffe" (Alfred Stieglitz, graphite) 4. Label: handwritten, "An American Place' / 509 Madison Ave —Room 1710 / (S.E. corner 53rd St) — New York"1 
(Source: Lynes, 1999)

other.content:
The 1996 examination report simply says “Line and Curve-27, O’Keeffe” without a “?” 
There was not an image available at the time of publishing to verify. (Source: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* from the NGA, 2025)

cr_data.provenance: The artist [1887-1986]; her estate; bequest 1987 to NGA. (Source: NGA, 2025)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Exam. at Amer. Place, March 1946. . . . No signature [notes backing inscription 2]. . . . Infor. from Miss Bry (An Amer. Place), July 1949: On permanent loan to the National Gallery of Art, Washington, from Georgia O'Keeffe as part of the Alfred Stieglitz Collection." Reproduced and titled *Black, Lavender and White* in *America & Alfred Stieglitz* (1934). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.notes: Source of title: backing inscription 2, Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks, 1940 and 1941 New York (An American Place–October) exhibition checklists.

description: A dark line runs through the center of a plain, purplish gray surface. A white, curved form pokes into the composition in the upper right corner.
